svg.aria-label: Diagram: AWS Quick now supports plugins to bundle agents, skills, connectors and flows. Plugins are bundles of capabilities that work together for a role, team, or task, packaging the agents, skills, connectors and flows that a job needs so you start from a ready setup instead of configuring each piece yourself, and installing a plugin sets up every capability it contains in one step. A plugin can contain up to 50 agents, skills, connectors, and flows. The four component types are agents, which are configurable AIs given instructions, knowledge sources and tools; skills, which are reusable instruction sets that teach agents how to complete a specific task; connectors, which are links that let Quick reach external applications and services so agents can access data and act on your behalf; and flows, which are multi-step workflows that automate repeatable tasks. The credential model is the reassuring part and it is explicit: sharing a connector in a plugin does not share your sign-in, each person signs in to the connector with their own account, and at install time if the plugin needs a connector you select an existing connector or create one before continuing to install. A flow also runs as the user who runs it and uses that user's access, so the bundle carries the shape of access rather than the access itself. The part to plan for is that install-time review is point-in-time. An installed plugin stays in sync with the owner's published version, so it updates automatically as the owner republishes, and publishing replaces the live version so everyone the plugin was shared with moves to the update. There is no version pinning and no re-review on update, so the set of agents, skills, connectors and flows you inspected before installing is not necessarily the set you are running later. The documented way to freeze a version is to duplicate the plugin, which creates a separate plugin that you own and therefore stops receiving the owner's updates, trading currency for control. Two further consequences of ownership: sharing a plugin also gives the people you share it with view access to the capabilities inside it, and deleting a plugin you own removes it permanently for everyone it is shared with. Uninstalling removes the capabilities the plugin installed unless a capability was installed separately or another installed plugin references it. Administrator control is a scope-down model: custom permissions is a policy applied at the account, role or user level that limits the capabilities people can use, it restricts capabilities and does not grant them, with a parent Plugins capability whose denial restricts the full feature set and a child capability covering sharing plugins with individuals. Finally, a test run takes real actions, so review the steps before running one. The capability is available in all Regions where AWS Quick is available.

svg.text: You review the bundle once. It keeps changing afterwards.
“An installed plugin stays in sync with the owner’s published version, so it updates automatically as
the owner republishes.”
Four capability types in one install, up to 50 items
agents configurable AIs with instructions, knowledge sources and tools
skills reusable instruction sets that teach agents a specific task
connectors reach external apps · “access data and act on your behalf”
flows multi-step workflows that automate repeatable tasks
The credential model is the good news, and it is explicit

with their own account.”

You inspect the agents, skills, connectors and flows before choosing Install. After that the owner
decides what the bundle contains, and the next republish arrives without a prompt.
To freeze it you Duplicate — which makes it yours, and stops the updates.

More than 100 skills and plugins at launch, with official bundles from AWS and trusted partners.
Available in all Regions where AWS Quick is available.
